slice.leaf: strict single-parent expected-predecessor CAS checkpoint protocol for two competing writers plus idempotent retry
slice.selection_reason: This is the highest-value continuation from r226 because it converts provider-anchored content-addressed lineage from passive duplicate/stale detection into an explicit conflict-rejecting recurrence protocol without hosted compute or protected authority.

observed_contract: Create-or-update requires the current blob sha when updating a file.
The endpoint exposes HTTP 409 Conflict as a possible failure class.
A successful contents update returns a commit object whose response includes parent commit identity.

candidates_compared.candidate: single mutable pointer file updated with expected current blob sha plus immutable checkpoint records

candidates_compared.conflict_duplication_risk: medium because lineage detects but does not itself serialize competing writers

candidates_compared.candidate: immutable unique checkpoint files without a CAS pointer
candidates_compared.conflict_duplication_risk: medium because duplicate payloads can be detected but a single current successor is not forced

two_writer_trace: Initial state: pointer file has blob p0 and names immutable checkpoint C0.
Writers A and B both read p0 and C0 before either writes.
A creates CA with prev=C0 and updates the pointer using expected sha=p0; under the contents-API model this is the unique transition from p0 to a new pointer blob p1.

B then presents stale expected sha=p0. Because the update contract requires the blob sha of the file being replaced while the current pointer is now p1, B is rejected as a conflict instead of overwriting A.
If A loses the response and retries, A first rereads the pointer. If operation_id and payload_digest already equal A's intended operation, the retry is classified as success without another write.
If B rereads after its conflict and sees another operation_id, B must stop or explicitly rebase from the new predecessor; it cannot silently reuse p0.
invariants: At most one logical successor can be accepted from one expected pointer blob under stale-sha rejection.
A response-loss retry is idempotent when operation_id plus payload_digest are checked before any retry write.
A stale writer cannot overwrite the current pointer without first acquiring the new current pointer identity.
The immutable checkpoint predecessor field makes the accepted linear chain replayable and lets a later reader reject a branch whose declared predecessor is not the pointer it observed.

slice.exact_tested_scope: A linear single-branch GitHub Contents-API model with one mutable pointer path, immutable checkpoint records, exact blob identities, two writers that begin from the same pointer blob, and idempotent response-loss retry. No merge DAG, force-push adversary, branch-protection assumption, signed provenance, or provider-independent retention is included.
scope_limits: This invocation did not spend an extra repository-write chain to live-probe a stale sha against the provider; stale-writer rejection is therefore model-level evidence grounded in the documented replacement-sha requirement and 409 conflict class, not a live 409 observation.
Provider trust, branch/ref mutability, force-push resistance, repository deletion, unreachable-object retention, and provider-independent authenticity remain unresolved children.

The protocol requires repository contents write permission but no hosted runner, Actions, Codespaces, artifact/LFS/package service, external executor, protected-primary authority, or manual user execution step.
